paras: The threatened lynching of Harry Hyath took place in Des Moines, Iowa, on or before 1 September 1881, when a crowd at police headquarters decided to lynch Hyath, a boarder who had been arrested for allegedly attempting to outrage a seven-year-old girl. Police quickly placed him in jail, and he was discharged at his examination when the girl was too frightened to testify. The episode is known only from a short wire paragraph that two Minnesota weeklies printed in their crime columns, and it does not give Hyath's race.

Hyath boarded at the Staffordshire house in Des Moines. According to the wire report, he enticed the proprietor's seven-year-old daughter into his room, locked the door and attempted to outrage her. Her screams brought her parents, who burst open the door, and Hyath fled.

Hyath was arrested and brought to police headquarters, where, in the report's words, "the crowd assembled decided to lynch him." He was "quickly placed in jail" instead, and no attempt to reach him there is reported. The report gives no date, hour or size for the crowd.
At Hyath's examination the girl was so frightened that she could not speak, and he was discharged. No later report on Hyath or on the crowd appears in the coverage.

The Worthington Advance and the Morris Tribune, both Minnesota papers, carried the same paragraph on 1 September 1881 under the heading "Record of Crime." The roundup placed it after reports of the hanging of two Black prisoners taken from a Louisiana jail and the mob killing of a Black man in Michigan. The paragraph stated the charge as fact, called Hyath "the rascal" and "the villian," and reported the crowd's decision to lynch him without comment. Unlike the items beside it, it identified no one by race, and no Des Moines paper's account was found.

No one was killed: a crowd that had gathered at police headquarters resolved to lynch Hyath over an alleged attempted outrage, but he was quickly placed in jail and later discharged (A1).
The only reports are one identical wire paragraph printed in two Minnesota papers on the same day (A1, A2); no Des Moines or independent account was found.
